title: Business Central Under the Hood episode 3: How Many Users Can Business Central Handle in the Cloud?

chapters.title: VM Load Thresholds and Capacity Management
Scaling Out and Scaling In Strategy
VM Provisioning Time and Performance Buffers
Performance Toolkit and Testing in Cloud

features.name: Virtual Machine Scale Set
features.description: Business Central cloud runs on Azure virtual machine scale sets with a cluster of VMs hosting both the web server and NST components. Clusters typically start with a minimum of five VMs and can scale up to 30 or more based on demand.
caveats: Architecture details are not publicly documented

features.name: Load Balancer
features.description: A load balancer understands Business Central sessions and routes requests to appropriate VMs. It monitors CPU load and other metrics to decide which VM handles each request. Existing UI sessions remain on the same VM, but new sessions are directed based on current load.

features.name: CPU Load Threshold at 60%
features.description: The system sets a 60% CPU load threshold for individual VMs. When a VM exceeds this threshold, the load balancer stops sending new sessions to it, allowing existing sessions to complete while new traffic routes to other VMs. The 60% threshold is a compromise between reaction time and efficient resource utilization.
caveats: Threshold may be tuned over time

features.name: Automatic VM Scale-Out
features.description: When all VMs in a cluster exceed the 60% threshold, the system automatically adds more VMs. This happens continuously and clusters can have practically infinite VMs in Azure cloud. Scale-out is done aggressively when needed.

features.name: Automatic VM Scale-In
features.description: After periods of high activity, VMs are gradually removed when the overall cluster has sustained low load for an extended time. Scale-in happens more slowly than scale-out to avoid aggressive capacity reductions.
caveats: Scale-in is intentionally slower than scale-out

features.name: Database Scaling and Monitoring
features.description: The system continuously monitors database CPU load, IO, data IO, and log IO metrics. When thresholds are exceeded, database capacity is automatically increased. An algorithm determines when and how much to scale the database.

features.name: In-client performance profiler
features.description: A built-in tool available in the product that any user can open without installation. Users can start the profiler, run a slow scenario, and stop to see timing details showing which methods and code are consuming time, with call stack views to pinpoint exact performance issues.

features.name: Database locks page
features.description: A page in the product that shows currently held locks and sessions waiting for locks. Users can refresh with F5 to get a point-in-time view of which users hold locks on which records and which triggers or code is responsible.

features.name: Database missing indexes page
features.description: A page that queries SQL for index recommendations. SQL Server monitors the database and performs thought experiments to recommend indexes that would improve performance and calculate the maintenance cost of those indexes.
caveats: requires running for several days to accumulate recommendations

features.name: Application insights telemetry
features.description: Integration with Microsoft Application Insights to monitor BC environments. The system emits events for SQL statements and other interesting activities. Partners can enable additional logging in a session to see all SQL statements being executed with timing details.
caveats: by default only emits SQL queries slower than 750 milliseconds to avoid overflowing the service

features.name: User scalability in Business Central cloud
features.description: Business Central can handle hundreds or thousands of concurrent users in the cloud through horizontal scaling. The main constraint is locking when multiple users work simultaneously, which depends on AL code optimization.
caveats: locking can become a bottleneck with many concurrent users
depends heavily on how AL code is written

features.name: Business Central scalability guide
features.description: A published guide containing real customer examples and scalability benchmarks, including examples like 5,000 sales invoices posted in one hour and information about API call capacity.
features.status_evidence_quote: scalability guide that we released recently we'll put some Link in the description so you can take a look at it

features.name: Performance toolkit
features.description: A toolkit for simulating what-if scenarios to test Business Central performance with specific user counts and workloads before deploying large customers to the cloud. Allows testing with up to 1,000 users.
caveats: requires cloud environment to run tests
